questions: Did line_loss_events fall to zero or near zero on the s-bend and slalom (1.0 each in iteration 1)?
Did max_error drop below 0.06 m on every track, and did any run still end off track?
Does the 16 mm footprint make the signal too coarse near centre (rms_error higher than the 0.025 to 0.033 m range seen so far)?
Is steering_oscillation above or below the 0.14 to 0.16 level? If above with no line loss, the next step is y = 0.05 m.
Does the robot complete any track? If it completes but completion_time is above 2 s, the next step is wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg.
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp value that gave the best rms_error with this 16 mm array, and which sensors carry most signal when on the line.

intent: Test whether a contiguous 16 mm footprint at 16 mm pitch (x = ±0.048 m) removes the s-bend and slalom line loss seen in iterations 0 and 1. Hold all other geometry constant so the result isolates the sensing change. Expect line_loss_events near 0 on all tracks, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress and completion to improve. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.16 with no line loss, the next lever is the forward offset (y = 0.05 m).
learning: Iteration 1 showed that widening the array with 12 mm footprints helped the oval (line loss 1.8 to 1.0) but not the s-bend or slalom. Those two tracks still lose the line once per run at about 4 cm error, so the footprint size, not only the span, limits detection. Iteration 1 also changed the controller (kp 4.0, weights proportional to x), so future comparisons must hold the controller fixed or report its effect separately. Remaining hypotheses: forward offset 0.05 m for oscillation (hypothesis 2), and wheel track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg for slalom turn rate and time (hypotheses 3 and 4).
rationale: Iteration 1 widened the array to seven 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch (x = ±0.036). Score fell from 64.7 to 50.7. Oval line loss improved (1.8 to 1.0), but s-bend and slalom still lose the line once per run (1.0 each), and max_error stays at 0.060 to 0.067 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Progress dropped on the oval (0.22 to 0.12). Integration feedback also changed the weights to be proportional to x and raised kp to 4.0, so the iteration 1 result mixes a span change with a controller change. Still, the geometry evidence is consistent: line loss persists on the two tracks where the robot leaves the tape, so the sensing footprint is still too narrow or too sparse at the edge. Body width cannot help, since the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for any allowed width. The Integrator's stated rule applies here: line loss above zero on the s-bend or slalom calls for the next step. I therefore set sensor_size to 0.016 m with seven sensors at 16 mm pitch, x = -0.048 to +0.048, y = 0.03. The 16 mm footprints tile contiguously, so the sum of readings should stay above 0.05 through the 4 to 5 cm error zone, and the outer edge moves to ±0.048 m. I hold wheel track (0.12 m), radius (0.03 m), mass (0.8 kg), body (0.12 x 0.16 m) and forward offset (0.03 m) fixed, so this race isolates the footprint and span change. Expected result: line_loss_events near zero on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 m, and the first completions on the oval or s-bend.
